dataList.name: Tangled Black Thread
dataList.desc: The effects of this unit's Skills, Low Morale, and Panic inflict [TangleBlackYarn] on the enemy ※ [TangleBlackYarn] can be reduced either by using Defense Skills or via certain Skills of this unit When hit, activate the following effects: - Gain 1 [SickBlackYarn] - If the Skill that hit this unit is a Slash Skill, gain 1 additional [SickBlackYarn] - If the Skill that hit this unit has 5+ Atk Weight, gain [HeavyBlackYarn] next turn (once per turn)
dataList.flavor:
The black thread wound around its body was not there before. By sheer fortune, when the previous age gave way to the next, those threads coiled around the body of the thing of eld. Wrapped in thread, it survived into the Age of the Department Store. Now, those black threads begin to come undone.

Before the Age of the Aquarium, came the Age of the Plaza, the Age of the Bomb Shelters, the Age of the Courtroom, and many others. Their names and forms may have differed, but the essence that drove the workings of the Sisyphe System remained ever the same.

With each passing Age, people adapted to the transformed world, enduring one era after another in their human form.

What lies tangled in the threads of the present Age is not merely that of the two preceding Ages, but every Age that has settled here, layer upon layer.

dataList.name: Alteration
dataList.desc: Turn Start: Inflict 1 [TailoringTarget] on the Sinner that dealt the most damage to this unit last turn and use the "Patterning" Skill - If the [TailoringTarget] Sinner has 9 [ScissorsMark], activate "Patterning" as "Surfile à la Chaîne" instead Every time this unit is hit by a Sinner, - Inflict 1 [ScissorsMark] on the said Sinner (max 5 per turn per Sinner) - Gain +1 [ChargeKhaki] Count (max 5 per turn per Sinner) Gain 3 [ResultEnhancement] every time this unit is hit by a Sinner that has [TailoringTarget] (max 9 per turn)
dataList.flavor:
They say a garment is only truly finished through alteration. Unless it was made to measure, it has to be adjusted until it fits the wearer.

And that is not true of clothing alone. Whatever is taken in from the outside must first be altered to suit oneself before it can be worn, lived in, and made to fit the heart.

dataList.name: Tailoring
dataList.desc: At Encounter Start or at the start of the turn this unit recovered from Stagger, gain 30 [FinishedFabric] Apply the [PanicChangeLock] effect Turn End: If this unit is in Panic, change SP to 30 Turn Start: - Gain Shield equal to ([FinishedFabric] Stack)% HP (max 30%) - Heal SP equal to [FinishedFabric] Stack
dataList.flavor:
Cutting means shaping fabric to a pattern. Cutting gives a garment its form, while alteration makes it wearable.

To fabric, then, cutting itself is a form of alteration. Once cut, the fabric takes on a shape that reflects its own properties, becoming the garment the cutter intended.

dataList.name: Scissors That Do Not Rest
dataList.desc: Every time Annette the Alterationist is hit by a Sinner, raise Stagger Threshold equal to 0.8% HP If this unit is Staggered, lose all Shield, [FinishedFabric], and [LargeTailoringShears]; then, gain 3 [Vulnerable] Turn Start: At 60% or less HP, - Gain 1 [ResultEnhancement] and 1 [SlashDamageUp] for every 20% missing HP (max 3 respectively) - Convert the final Coin of "Trimming" and Coin 2 of "Cutting" to [SuperCoin]
dataList.flavor:
A body whose very worth was shaped by the work of alteration goes on cutting without end, driven to alter and tailor forever.

Even as the body breaks apart, she cannot bring herself to stop altering and cutting. She is made to cut things away, yet cannot cut herself free.

Demand has gone through the roof, while raw hides have only grown harder to come by. The hide of the original sinners was once the sort nobody would so much as glance at. Then one season changed everything: demand surged, prices soared, and what used to be sold for scraps or simply thrown away became coveted material.

Now even the blemishes on its surface are dressed up as character and sold as part of the appeal.

dataList.name: Unending, Unavoidable Stream of Customer Complaints
dataList.desc:
"Cry of the Cocoon" is heard every "multiple of 3" turns
Upon entering Phase 2, "Cry of the Cocoon" continues to be heard every turn

This unit cannot be immobilized in the turn "Cry of the Cocoon" is heard

If this unit's HP is brought past its Stagger Threshold, gain 2 [Vulnerable] next turn
dataList.flavor:
Voices seep from the cocoon.

"Anything under 80-count two-ply? Not even fabric!"
"Why aren't the buttonholes horizontal?"
"Jersey knit on machine? Really?"
"Why isn't the selvage red?"
"This hasn't even been shrink-proofed."
"Anything below Super 150 is cheap cloth, obviously."
"You think the Super scale is just yarn thickness? Diameter and yarn count aren't even the same thing. Don't you know that?"
"You're finishing the hem with a Union Special, right? Of course you are!"
"Is this Rigid? ... Oh. Selvage?"
"Wait... the stitch-per-inch count is way too even. You used a machine, didn't you?"
"It's not bespoke if it's not hand-stitched."
"... That's not even a Milanese buttonhole."
"Shirting needs to be over 200-count."
"Ugh, I can see the stitching on the outside."
"There, I can see two rows of stitching there. Rejected."
"What's with this seam finish?"
"Three-ply, minimum."
